object_description: two long slender school volumes with stepped ends
design_condition: The two buildings are placed along the northern park edge and accommodate the terrain while freeing the park center, but their full-length occupation and southern facades dominate the open space.

positive.statement: The attempt to free up the center of the park by setting the school building to the side is appreciated.

position.rationale: Central open gap between the two diagonal school volumes approximates the freed park center.

positive.statement: The two-building arrangement accommodates the height differences in the terrain relatively elegantly.

position.rationale: Two elongated, staggered volumes are clearly visible across the plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The buildings remain noticeable as only one storey toward the northern neighborhood while retaining clear views.

position.rationale: Northern portions of the upper building approximate the neighborhood-facing low-scale edge.

positive.statement: The internal clear structure corresponds to the stringent construction principle and provides high flexibility of use.

position.rationale: Interior structure is not exposed; the marker is constrained to the upper elongated school volume.

positive.statement: The wooden construction, simple basic structure and flexibility of use take sustainability requirements into account.

position.rationale: Material is not distinguishable; placement marks the lower school volume as a representative construction anchor.

positive.statement: The idea of uniting gardeners and athletes through shared infrastructure is socially stimulating.

position.rationale: The inter-building gap is the plausible shared zone between the two visible school volumes.

negative.statement: The open space is overdeveloped by four parallel paths, while a clear path concept is not recognizable.

position.rationale: Open space between and around the parallel buildings approximates the criticized path network.

negative.statement: There are hardly any places to stay away from, and the required diversity of play spaces is missing.

position.rationale: No play-space geometry is distinguishable; the marker indicates the adjacent open-space region.

negative.statement: The school lacks a main entrance and therefore a clear address because of its longitudinal orientation and access on all sides.

position.rationale: No entrance is visible; the southern edge provides a constrained facade anchor.

negative.statement: The sports field and southern school facades dominate the park, leaving landscape areas only as fragments.

position.rationale: Long southern edges of the diagonal volumes visibly face the open central area.

negative.statement: The division of the program into two buildings is operationally suboptimal because movement between them occurs through uncovered outdoor space.

position.rationale: The clear gap separating the two building masses is directly visible in plan.

negative.statement: The separation of the all-day school and regular school makes future expansion of the all-day offer difficult.

position.rationale: The model clearly shows two distinct, disconnected elongated school volumes.

negative.statement: The corridors have little daylight, lack spatial quality and cannot adequately absorb the expected number of students.

position.rationale: Interior corridors are not visible; the marker is placed within the upper building footprint.

negative.statement: The schematic repetition of the external expression lacks expressiveness.

position.rationale: Repeated stepped and parallel outer edges visibly support a schematic facade-expression anchor.

negative.statement: The proposed building-services rooms are far too small.

position.rationale: Services rooms are absent internally; the lower building footprint supplies a constrained location.

negative.statement: The creation costs reach the top of the ranked projects.

position.rationale: Cost ranking has no useful spatial referent in the sampled geometry.

negative.statement: The proposal occupies too much park space and becomes a school park rather than a school in the park.

position.rationale: The two long school masses occupy a substantial portion of the visible site plan.
